feeds.title: Childhood101
feeds.description: Childhood 101 was founded in 2009 by award-winning teacher and author, Christie Burnett. At Childhood 101 we are dedicated to inspiring parents, teachers and other caregivers to create playful learning opportunities in their homes and learning environments with children aged 2-12. Find activities and experiences to inspire you in your interactions with children at home, school or as a carer or educator of young children.

feeds.title: Activity Village Blog
feeds.description: Activity Village offers teachers, parents and children from all over the world over 10,000 pages of free children's activities - simply explore, enjoy, make and print! You will find coloring pages, kids crafts and printable activities for children including puzzles, sudoku for kids, educational resources, homeschool resources and much more!

feeds.title: Hands On As We Grow
feeds.description: Hi! I am Jamie Reimer the author of this blog. Hands On As We Grow is all about learning to do hands-on activities with your kids. I share lots of practical, easy activities, and sneak in learning opportunities. You'll find here crafts, art projects, gross motor activities, and fine motor activities regularly.

feeds.title: Totschooling
feeds.description: Totschooling is a blogging mom to a toddler and a preschooler, sharing ideas and resources for early education. On her blog, you will find free printables for toddlers, alphabet games, counting, puzzles, pre-writing, scissor skills, math & literacy.

feeds.title: Living Montessori Now
feeds.description: My name is Deb Chitwood. A former Montessori teacher and school owner with a master's degree in early childhood studies. I also homeschool my kids through high school. Now I write about Montessori activities and ideas, homeschooling and parenting in general.

feeds.title: Little Bug Lovers
feeds.description: Little Bug Lovers is a new niche blog for young children that is very different. It's a place to learn all about Bugs and Insects. Written in a child-friendly language with lots of vibrant imagery. I've also started to add insect-based art lessons. I plan to add coloring pages, and even online games about Bugs and build a community with kids, parents, and teachers in this wonderful niche.

feeds.title: KidFriendly DC
feeds.description: A go-to resource for recreation with kids in the DC-Metro area.

feeds.title: Storypark
feeds.description: This blog is where Storypark and its community of inspiring educators and parents share their thoughts, resources and tips. Our aim is to help every child fulfil their unique potential, by connecting and empowering the community around them.

feeds.title: Fun Learning for Kids Blog
feeds.description: Hi, my name is Danielle! We have tons of engaging and effective learning activities and free printables. You will find alphabet activities, number sense activities, science experiments, math and literacy centers and lots more hands-on learning!

feeds.title: TinkerLab
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Rachelle Doorley. The TinkerLab Blog chronicles my journey as a maker mom you can read my very first post here and it's also a great place to hunt for science projects, art activities, invitations to create, and the ongoing TinkerSketch Challenges.

feeds.title: Pre Kinders Blog
feeds.description: I'm Karen Cox, a Pre-K teacher in Georgia. If you are looking for teaching ideas and printable activities to help you teach Pre-K, you are in the right place. This site is a place where I share lessons and ideas I use in my Pre-K classroom: everything from math to literacy, fine motor to classroom management. I enjoy creating hands-on printable learning materials, and I share many of those here.

feeds.title: The Spoke
feeds.description: Early Childhood Australia advocates to ensure quality, social justice and equity in all issues relating to the education and care of children from birth to eight years. Every young child is thriving and learning Our role in achieving this vision is to be an effective advocate for young children and a champion for quality outcomes in early childhood education and care.

feeds.title: Teach Mama
feeds.description: Amy Kilpatrick Mascott is the creator of teachmama.com, where since 2008, she has shared tools and resources parents can use to become the best teachers they can be for their children.

feeds.title: Teachstone Blog
feeds.description: Explore resources for teachers, coaches, and observers and learn about CLASS and effective interactions on our blog. As the trusted leader in CLASS-driven measurement and mentoring, Teachstone has the proven expertise schools need to nurture better student outcomes, one classroom at a time. With decades of early childhood education research as a foundation, we offer products and programs that help schools unlock the potential of great teachers, boost student outcomes, and create a culture of sustained excellence.

feeds.title: 1+1+1=1 Blog
feeds.description: 1+1+1=1 is owned and written by me, Carisa Hinson. If you are a parent, a homeschooler, a classroom teacher, or anyone who works with children - you are in the right place! At 1Plus1Plus1Equals1, Carisa Hinson offers printables to use in the classroom.

feeds.title: The Activity Mom - Sharing Activities and Ideas that Make Learning Fun
feeds.description: Nicole, Mom to a 8 year old son and 5 year old daughter. Before staying home with her two children, Nicole taught 5th grade, 4th grade, and then became a Reading Interventionist. Nicole has a degree in Elementary Education and a Masters Degree in Teaching and Learning. Interactive activity kits filled with hands on learning targeted toward toddler and preschool age children.

feeds.title: Teacher Tom
feeds.description: A blog about teaching and learning from preschoolers. Thomas Hobson is a preschool teacher & author of Teacher Tom's First Book. He is inspired by the idea of helping thousands of educators to take their financial futures into their own hands almost as much as the idea of creating thousands of high-quality preschools.

feeds.title: Just Family Fun
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Gavin, forklift driver at a yogurt factory, dad to a gorgeous 6-year-old, and creator of Just Family Fun! I designed this site, its games, activities, and worksheets to help parents and teachers, everywhere. My goal is to banish boredom, brighten rainy days and get kids to love learning.

feeds.title: Sharing Kindergarten Blog
feeds.description: I'm Mary, a Kindergarten teacher from Georgia. I am a learner. I have a Bachelors and Masters degree in early childhood education as well as a specialist degree in Instructional Technology. I adore my small family. I love blogging, creating games, and instructing little minds. Teaching is my life's passion.

feeds.title: Early Childhood Ireland Blog
feeds.description: Early Childhood Ireland is a membership-based organisation focused on the comprehensive provision of early years childcare and education in Ireland

feeds.title: An Apple For The Teacher
feeds.description: Hi! I'm Kelly Malloy! I'm a curriculum developer and Teachers pay Teachers Seller. On my blog, An Apple for the Teacher, I share classroom tips, teaching ideas and upper elementary classroom resources. I currently teach 4th grade.

feeds.title: All My Children Blog
feeds.description: At All My Children, we believe that early childhood years are the most important in a child's life. We are committed to the continuous customization of performance standards of early childhood development. Our mission at is to enrich the life's of children by facilitating the opportunity to grow, learn, and play in a structured but fun loving environment.

feeds.title: Adventures in a Messy Life
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Ticia! This is the adventures of my family in life and learning. At Adventures in Mommydom, you'll find ways to make your school more interactive and encouragement for you as you parent your kids. Together we can not just survive as parents and teachers, but thrive.

feeds.title: Blooming early years
feeds.description: Our main focus is to help you create learning environments that educate, engage and inspire. We appreciate that your time as teachers or parents is precious and can be difficult to find high quality teaching resources, so we here to make your life a bit easier by creating materials that will educate, inspire and enable you to focus more of your time and energy on inspiring lifelong blooming journeys of learner.

feeds.title: Cara Carroll
feeds.description: My name is Cara Carroll. In my current role as an educational consultant, I love helping teachers whether it be through meaningful & engaging professional development, mentoring, one-on-one consulting, or even just an encouraging smile and a pat on the back.

feeds.title: Eye on Early Childhood
feeds.description: Eye on Early Childhood is a blog hosted by Strategies for Children. They post about the early childhood practices, policies, and research that help children and their families thrive. They share the voices of families, early educators, advocates, and policymakers. Their blogger, Alyssa Haywoode, is a former journalist who wrote editorials for The Des Moines Register and The Boston Globe.

feeds.title: Kids News and Reviews
feeds.description: Interactive blog where children and youth share their stories focused on early learning and social responsibility. Editorial content is written by children and their teachers with the editorial guidance of our editor/publisher, Lorrie Holmes.

feeds.title: Takoma Park Cooperative Nursery School Blog
feeds.description: At The Cooperative School, we've created four distinct spaces which lead the experiences offered in each. Our Four Spaces for Learning include the Classroom, Project Center, Imagination Station, and our Outdoor Play Space. Our unique space and curriculum are intentionally designed by our director, Lesley Romanoff.

feeds.title: Marcia Hebert's Blog
feeds.description: For the last 25+ years, I have been a successful teacher, director, and leader in the field of early childhood education. My blog posts, my consulting and coaching services, along with my broad array of training and workshops for early childhood educators offer a wealth of best practice materials and resources for those who aspire to quality in the field. Thank you for visiting! I invite you to share your thoughts and look forward to hearing from you.

feeds.title: Jemima's Playhouse Blog
feeds.description: Jemima's Playhouse is a multicultural program that provides interesting workshops for preschool and primary aged children.

feeds.title: Joyful Learning in the Early Years
feeds.description: I am a Reggio Emilia inspired Full Day Kindergarten teacher and mother to three young children. This blog is meant as a communication tool for the families of our children and as a learning tool for the many educators who follow us.

feeds.title: Kaplan Early Learning Company Blog
feeds.description: Kaplan Early Learning Co. offers innovative products, cutting-edge curricula/assessments, resources and information for educators, caregivers and parents.

feeds.title: Nursery World
feeds.description: Nursery World is the leading title for the early years community, in print and online. Discover, share and discuss all the latest news and best practice about early years education and childcare with us.

feeds.title: Teach Preschool Blog
feeds.description: Deborah J. Stewart writes about her observations and reflections on early childhood education, covering literacy, art, STEM, sensory play, and motor skills. Deborah holds an associate degree and a master's degree in Early Childhood Education. She has served in a broad range of roles in early childhood education over her 30 years including teaching in the classroom, serving as School Director, Curriculum Development, Professional Development Training, and Musical Director.

feeds.title: The Imagination Tree
feeds.description: In this site, you will find plenty of ideas for art and crafts, imaginative play, creativity, science investigations, early maths ideas and LOTS of fun. She hopes, readers will be inspired with hundreds of ideas for creative play and learning for kids.

feeds.title: Kinedu Blog | Baby Development
feeds.description: Kinedu is an app which allows you to harness the learning potential of your child's early years with a personalised plan for directed play and real-life interactions.

feeds.title: What the Teacher Wants!
feeds.description: What the Teacher Wants was started in 2010 as a way for Rachelle to post pictures of her classroom and share her teaching ideas. We share teaching ideas for the K-6th grade classrooms to make life easier for the teacher and learning fun for the students!

feeds.title: Happy Hooligans
feeds.description: I'm Jackie Currie, the creative spirit behind Happy Hooligans. I'm a mom, a wife, a daycare provider, and a self-proclaimed glitter phone. I'm working on that last bit and making progress. Here you will find kids' crafts, kids' activities, crafts and activities for toddlers, preschoolers, elementary students, tweens and teens, home daycare activities, easy recipes, and parenting advice.

feeds.title: Preschool Inspirations
feeds.description: I'm Katie. My degree is in Early Childhood Education, and I have been able to help children worldwide while working with sponsorship programs in India (with World Vision) and Romania (with One Child Matters). I'm sharing my best play recipes, teacher tips, & learning activities with a sprinkling of real life!

feeds.title: Confidence Meets Parenting
feeds.description: This blog started as A Mom with a Lesson Plan. It was a way for me to share some of the fun things I was doing with my own kids. With a background in Early Childhood, I knew I had something special to share with other parents. What I didn't expect was all the learning I would be doing along the way.

feeds.title: Teach Kids Art Blog
feeds.description: I'm Cheryl, and I'm a great supporter of children's art. I spent over 20 years teaching art to children and it was the most rewarding job I've ever had! This diverse set of experiences has taught me a lot, and I'm happy to keep sharing what I've learned in order to assist others find success teaching art to children!

feeds.title: Fun in First
feeds.description: Hi! I'm Jodi and I'm a 1st grade teacher in Indiana.I am currently in my 16th year of teaching. My first job was as an Art teacher. This was not my major, minor or endorsement, but it was a job and it got my foot in the door. This gave me great experience working with Kindergarten through 5th Grade students, and it allowed me to use my creative side.

feeds.title: Cheqdin
feeds.description: The Next Generation Childcare Software & App for Nurseries, Out of School Clubs, Preschools & Childminders. Proudly helping the global early years community.

feeds.title: Can Cubs
feeds.description: Our blog brings you the best information relating to education, health, technology, news and much more! Whether you're a parent or an educator you're bound to find something useful here.

feeds.title: Roots and Wings
feeds.description: This blog features one teacher's approach to kindergarten, inspired by the early childhood practices of Reggio, Montessori, and Waldorf, but applied to a public school setting. I am passionate about project work, inquiry-based learning, STEAM education, nature study and preparing my littles for the future. Visit the free resource library found on the homepage for lots of kindergarten goodness!

feeds.title: Early Childhood Master's Education
feeds.description: The latest news and updates on early childhood education by Shimane, a 30 years old and Assistant Teacher at an Early Childhood Learning Center.

feeds.title: Music in the Early Years
feeds.description: Musical Help, Ideas and Training for Early Years Practitioners and for those wishing to start their own Under 5s Music Business.

feeds.title: TinyIvy
feeds.description: Stay up to date with the latest advances in literacy research and the science of reading. Learn how to teach your child to read by using the TinyIvy Phonics System.

feeds.title: Kids English College
feeds.description: KidsEnglishCollege™ offers tools that allow educators to quickly teach children aged 1 to 7 years of age a large collection of new words and instinctively recognize correct grammar rules.

feeds.title: Early Years Staffroom
feeds.description: A community for Early Years Professionals. We share our knowledge so you save your time.

feeds.title: Creative Connections For Kids by Kristi Delp
feeds.description: Kristi Delp is the coordinator and parent educator for Parents as Teachers (PAT) and the manager of this blog. Equipped with a master's degree in early childhood special education and 20 years of experience, she shares valuable advice and insight on everything from fun family recipes and parenting tips to games and activities that develop motor skills.

feeds.title: WECA | Because Small Lives Get Bigger
feeds.description: A blog from the Wisconsin Early Childhood Association. Wisconsin Early Childhood Association (WECA) is a statewide, nonprofit organization serving as a professional association whose members care for and educate Wisconsin's children, aged birth to eight. We are an affilliate of the National Association for the Education of Young Children (NAEYC).

feeds.title: FTKny.com | Early Childhood Education Blog
feeds.description: FTKny.com has the largest selection of educational enrichment, preschool, gifted & talented and tutoring programs for children ages 2 -14 in the NYC metropolitan area.

feeds.title: Early Learning Childhood Education
feeds.description: The Bonkers Beat Music Program was created in 2006, Melbourne and has already achieved amazing results in children's learning and development.

feeds.title: Happenings With Hemme
feeds.description: Articles on Early childhood education, preschool, and much more.

feeds.title: Inverloch Childcare Blog
feeds.description: At Inverloch Childcare we work in partnership with our community, our families and our employees to provide a sustainable, high quality early childhood education service where each child, their family and their cultural and social context is valued and respected.

feeds.title: Kindertown Education Blog by Lanette Gemmill
feeds.description: At Kindertown Education Blog, Find the Best Educational Apps for Preschoolers. Every app in KinderTown has been reviewed by early childhood educators so for the first time, parents can browse for apps knowing every app is not only engaging, but has significant educational value.

feeds.title: Childventures Early Learning Academy Blog
feeds.description: Childventures Early Learning Academy offers a network of leading childcare centres for preschool & daycare in Vaughan, Richmond Hill, Ancaster, Thornhill & Burlington. Our children are offered the highest quality childcare services & instill in young minds the importance of moral values & character formation. Get the latest updates about Childventures by signing up for our blog.

feeds.title: Teach123 | Lessons And Tips For Primary Teachers
feeds.description: I've taught in schools as small as 300 students and as large as 2,000 students, both public and private school, from a Title I school to schools where funds were readily available. From this wide range of experiences I've gained wonderful insights of a broad spectrum of what education is all about. You will find my lessons and materials are an accumulation of my experiences.

feeds.title: Teach Preschool Blog
feeds.description: Deborah J. Stewart, M.Ed. has invested over 30 years in the field of early childhood education. She owns her own small private preschool called The Children's Studio for children ages three to five years old. Deborah's preschool is her place to observe, document, and study early learning in action. She shares her observations and reflections on early childhood education with others.

feeds.title: Topics in Early Childhood Education
feeds.description: John Funk has worked in early childhood since 1979. He taught preschool, 1st and 2nd grades and kindergarten. He worked as an early childhood specialist for a large school district and managed early childhood services for Salt Lake CAP Head Start.

feeds.title: Pondering Preschool
feeds.description: I see this blog as a dwelling place for my enthusiasm for 'all things early childhood'. This blog is a soft place for teachers, parents, and caregivers to land, to consider a variety of educational topics, and perhaps help us understand little ones.

feeds.title: Teach Junkie
feeds.description: Welcome to the place for teachers to share bright ideas, creative lesson plans and activities! Teach Junkie is proud to promote the work of teachers.

feeds.title: Pre-K Pages Blog
feeds.description: I'm Vanessa Levin, an early childhood teacher, consultant, public speaker, and author. I have started the Pre-K Pages as a resource site for Pre-K and preschool teachers. Pre-K Pages offers printable lesson plans and playful learning themes for Preschool, Pre-K, and Kindergarten kids with fun hands-on activities.

feeds.title: Kids Activities Blog
feeds.description: Kids Activities is a blog by Holly Harner based in United States which is a place where you can find inspiration and realistic ideas for more fun. Kids Activities Blog has kids crafts, kids activities and fun things to do with kids along with tips and tricks for parents.

feeds.title: Ed's Lessons Blog
feeds.description: Enjoy a browse through an illuminating collection of articles on the Ed's Lessons Blog. Ed's Lessons is a blog by Edwina, an Early Childhood educator, to help carers, parents and educators, effortlessly incorporate activities inspired by picture books and nature so that children not only develop much-needed and valued curiosity and a love for learning.

feeds.title: BOLD
feeds.description: The blog 'BOLD - Blog on Learning and Development' is an interdisciplinary initiative powered by the Jacobs Foundation. It is dedicated to spreading the word about learning, child development and youth development.

feeds.title: Miss Kindergarten - A kindergarten teaching Blog
feeds.description: Hadar is a kindergarten teacher and author of Miss Kindergarten blog.She taught kindergarten, 1st, 2nd and 3rd grade students. She loves blogging, crafting, creating and bargain shopping.

feeds.title: Defending the Early Years (DEY)
feeds.description: Denisha Jones, Ph.D., J.D., DEY's Co-Director, writes a monthly blog on current topics in early childhood education & advocacy. She writes articles on a variety of topics including Children & Technology, Child Development, Education Reform, Assessment, and Teacher Training.

feeds.title: HiMama Blog
feeds.description: HiMama is made up of a group of committed professionals, parents, daughters, sons, uncles and aunts who are working hard to build a product and a company that families and early childhood educators love. Looking for resources for your daycare center? HiMama's early childhood education blog is curated for childcare owners, directors and teachers. Check it out.

feeds.title: Taylor & Francis | Journal of Early Childhood Teacher Education
feeds.description: An international publisher covering bioscience, biotechnology and biochemistry. A Journal of Early Childhood Teacher Education.

feeds.title: Differentiated Kindergarten
feeds.description: Welcome to Differentiated Kindergarten! I'm Marsha, a teacher-mom committed to the journey of creating a differentiated classroom for my students. It's my goal to meet the needs of all my students through fun, engaging and developmentally appropriate activities.

feeds.title: Sparkles! Early Learning Academy Blog
feeds.description: Sparkles! Child Care Centers provide a safe learning environment while offering parents flexibility and peace of mind. Our roots in family home day care uniquely qualifies us to provide care that feels like an extension of the home with the added component of our educational curriculum.

feeds.title: Early Learning Management
feeds.description: Early Learning Management offers Childhood management services & solutions like Child Care Licensing, Operational Services, Project Management in Queensland.

feeds.title: Teach. Train. Love
feeds.description: TeachTrainLove.com is a community for educators who are committed to professional learning and passionate about the social, emotional, and academic growth of young learners.
